newsitem.title: CHINA: China firms Jan-Nov tax arrears up 72.9 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China firms Jan-Nov tax arrears up 72.9 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Chinese companies owed 35.7 billion yuan ($4.3 billion) in industrial and commercial taxes in the first 11 months of 1996, up 72.9 percent from the year-ago period, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
Tax agencies nationwide have been urged to make greater efforts to collect back taxes to ensure the tax collection target for the whole year is met, Xinhua said.
The State General Administration of Taxation blamed the rise in overdue tax payments on inefficient tax collection, a lack of funds and unscrupulous enterprises, Xinhua said.
Some companies have intentionally delayed tax payments by setting up dummy firms to avoid payments, it said.
Some enterprises grouped together and agreed in private not to be the first to pay taxes, the agency said.
"To solve these problems, we must develop better measures and improve law enforcement," a tax official said.
Finance Minister Liu Zhongli urged tax departments to cut the amount of overdue tax by 20 percent next year, the agency said.
China collected 563.9 billion yuan in industrial and commercial taxes in the first 11 months, up 19.5 percent from the year-ago period. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
